stem.text: Let p and q be continuous functions with \( \int_{-1}^{5} p(x)\,dx = 7 \), \( \int_{2}^{5} p(x)\,dx = -3 \), and \( \int_{2}^{-1} q(x)\,dx = 6 \). Find the value of \( \int_{-1}^{2} \left(2p(x) + 3q(x)\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Reverse the given integral of q: \( \int_{-1}^{2} q(x)\,dx = -(6) = -6 \), and use linearity on the requested integral.

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, one supplied integral runs right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: a linear combination of two functions

distractor_derivations.B: given integral of q from 2 to -1 used as if it ran from -1 to 2
distractor_derivations.C: split written with its limits reversed, taking the integral of p from -1 to 2 as -3 - (7)
distractor_derivations.D: integral of p from 5 to 2 taken as -3 instead of 3
